> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

Verified against the exact reviewed head `17594d4a6534c142cae764772fc42049e898eca3`: [the Linux JS job](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/actions/runs/34467004187/job/102837808254) loaded `sharp@0.35.4`, reported libvips `8.18.6`, generated a PNG and passed the trailing lockfile/manifest no-drift check. The version assertion executed successfully.

The SRI-verified [published sharp 0.35.4 package](https://registry.npmjs.org/sharp/-/sharp-0.35.4.tgz) sets `versions.sharp = pkg.version` in `dist/utility.cjs` and exposes it through `Sharp.versions`. Its export map does not expose `sharp/package.json`, so the suggested replacement is not compatible with this release. The current code uses the supported API; this finding is resolved by the source and actual CI evidence.

For the two suppressed suggestions: both consumer manifests are present in `pull_request.paths`, and parsed-workflow checks plus executed removal controls verified their coverage. Both committed frontend minima are `^15.5.24`; the lock and actual installed workspace trees resolve `15.5.24`. `npm ls` supplies installed-version evidence, alongside the pinned install and no-drift check. The independent Opus 5 review approved this concrete patched graph and classified the persistent trigger assertion as a nonblocking suggestion. A maintained anti-downgrade floor is a separate future policy suggestion; no individual Opus disposition is claimed for that suggestion. The current paths and declared, locked and installed versions have all been verified.
